children: Wage settlements awarded by British employers showed a bigger annual rise in the three months to the end of October but look set to fall further behind inflation in the months ahead, human resources data firm Brightmine said on Wednesday.
The median pay award by employers edged up to 3.2%, up from 3% in the previous three-month periods to September, August and July but smaller than raises seen earlier this year.

On Tuesday, official data showed pay growth excluding bonuses slowed to 3.5% in the three months to September, higher than the level most Bank of England policymakers view as inconsistent with sustainably returning inflation to its 2% target. Investors are pricing in another interest rate hike in December.
Nearly half of firms offered pay deals between 3% and 3.5%
Most deals did not exceed those given in 2025 and pay awards were expected to stay at 3% in 2027
Higher employer social security contributions and a 3.9% increase in the minimum wage could constrain how much firms raise median pay next year, Brightmine said
"As (the) minimum wage rises faster than pay awards, salary gaps could narrow, creating challenges around pay progression and morale, said Sheila Attwood, HR insights and data lead at Brightmine
Brightmine analysed 31 pay settlements between August 1 and October 31 covering around 850,000 employees including many public-sector workers who got pay rises of 3.5%-3.8%
